speaker: sefa
_comment: Entry nodes are tried in order; the first whose 'when' passes opens the conversation.

lines: She does not look up from the bed she is turning over.
"You are three years late and the wrong shape for a supply drone. Which are you?"
"Sefa Odim. Botanist. I came out on the second landing, found the place empty, and stayed because somebody had to keep the terrace from going to glass."
"That is the question, is it not."
"Eleven people. No bodies, no wreckage, no distress call. Beds made. Tools racked. The recycler switched off from the inside."
"Rike thinks it was a fault cascade. Nnenna does not say what she thinks, which is its own answer."
"Me, I keep finding their handwriting in the seed trays and I would like to know what they were so sure about."
"Rike came out a year after me. Nnenna last spring. Three of us rattling around a station built for eleven."
"It is not lonely exactly. It is more that the place feels borrowed."
"Everything. Start with the soil - it is the only thing here that pays you back on a schedule."
"Break a bed with the blade, put a lumen pod in it, water it every single day. Three days and you will have light in your hand."
"Then go and see Rike about the recycler. I would rather not spend another winter tasting the air."
"Since you are here and apparently useful."
"My glassroot line keeps failing in the fourth generation. Every batch comes up threaded with filament I did not put there, and then it collapses."
"I need three clean tubers to start again from. Grown, not scavenged."

choices.text: I will grow them for you.

lines: "That is what I would like to know. Sterile substrate, sealed trays, filtered water."
"And still, every time, something already living gets there first."

choices.text: I will grow you three clean ones.

lines: "Glassroot. Five days, water every one of them, and it will die on you if you forget twice."
"Three tubers. I will know if you dug them out of the hollow instead."
"Suit yourself. The trays are not going anywhere."
"Three glassroot. Clean ones. Water them like you mean it."
She straightens up when she sees you, which she does not usually bother with.
"You got the recycler up. I could taste the difference before I heard the fan."
"Odd thing, though. The terrace beds went quiet the same afternoon. Less give in the soil. I am probably imagining it."
"I am probably imagining it," she says again, to herself.
"I am going to tell you something I have not written down."

"The filament in my trays is not contamination. I have sequenced it four times. It is the same organism as the mat under the terrace, and it is everywhere - the beds, the drains, the dust in the hab filters."
"It is not growing into my cultures. It is already there, and my cultures are growing into it."
"Whatever the old crew were doing out here, they were not farming on top of a dead rock. They were farming on top of something."
"You found all of it, then."
"Six to five. They ended a colony on six to five."
"I have been turning that soil for four years and I never once asked it what it wanted. Ask me again in a week what I think we should do. I do not have it yet."
"Water first, questions after."
"The blade breaks the bed, the canister wets it, and nothing at all happens unless you come back tomorrow and do it again."
